doc.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11

title: The red light district, supervised cabarets and tips
summary: How the district was divided, how Sbarbaro's side was run, and pay by tips.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: that was a little lower rate well we played on the rampart street separated one section which was the red light and the cabarets and you couldn't you couldn't uh you couldn't walk in those days the girls couldn't walk across that track they'd be picked up unless they were saying well I'm going to the store and they had a good reason because they never allowed them out of the section yeah you never
never used to see them because the women smoked and the places where we were at was run real nice

but it was the women were sitting there everyone in our place was a singer or thought she could sing let's put it that way you know what I mean but on the other side i'm afraid it was run a little bit more like a sailor could walk in there and do anything you want long as he spent the money but you couldn't do that on couldn't do that no on our side none of the girls were turning tricks in your place oh sure everything is done in a different way on the other place you see more fights break out more trouble but you never saw any trouble on this side because it was supervised properly you know run right at the same time if a man buys a gal a bottle of champagne that was the old come on those days she'd take him upstairs well all right there was no but on the other side she'd she'd walk out so he'd go running after looking for her and the trouble started i didn't stay over on the other side too long i found out that
i see the band too when the band played and then then they'd come around past the tray around the table
you know the tips you made good money in tips in those yeah they should be all right because you got a

you got about a buck and a half a night to play i don't think anybody got over two dollars so you'd depend on tips you'd get some you'd get some fellas would take the thing and throw it on the floor would be insulted and you get some of them that would put some change in there it happens
